commit.message:
mlx: the menu bar icon shows the startup phase (starting/warming) while the model loads

serve/server.py writes a small strata-status.json (loading -> warming -> ready); the mlx warmup marks warming; the menu bar reads it and shows 'Strata — starting…'/'warming up…' until /health answers.

mlx: warmup option, so the first chat does not pay MLX's kernel compilation

The model already loads at startup; warmup adds one short generation so MLX compiles its Metal kernels and allocates the KV/workspace then. Off by default; the shipped configs set warmup: true. The engine cache is reset after, so the first request is unaffected.
docs: rewrite the README for this Apple Silicon (MLX) fork

Apple Silicon (MLX) backend: run small GGUF/HF models on the Mac

Adds an in-process Metal backend behind a backend registry, so Strata's server, web app and API can serve a small/medium quantized model without CUDA/HIP.

- serve/backends/: registry + mlx.py (mlx-lm, quantized KV cache, cross-turn prefix reuse) + hf_tokenizer.py (a Hugging Face tokenizer behind the server's tokenizer interface)
- serve/server.py, serve/frontend.py: --engine backend plugins, JSON tool calls (Qwen2.5), ChatTemplate(source=...)
- serve/extract.py + POST /v1/extract: attach a PDF as text in the web app
- serve/telemetry.py: Apple Silicon GPU/memory readings for the Monitor
- serve/web: PDF attachments, a document-context note, favicon
- macOS: setup-macos.sh, run-macos.sh, menu bar icon (strata-menubar.command, install-menubar.sh), docs/MACOS_MLX.md, example run configs
- tests: serve/test_mlx_backend.py, serve/test_extract.py

serve: a tool call inside a code fence or inline code in the visible answer is text (#1058)

The live smoke showed the same quoted-example problem in the answer: a model that wrote the call format in a
fenced example after </think> got a real tool call. The content parser now uses the fence / inline-code
tracking of the reasoning rescue: an opener inside a ``` or ~~~ fence (tracked across stream chunks) or inside
inline code stays text, the decision depending only on the text before it, so streamed and whole outputs agree.
Openers at the top level fire as before, including one after a sentence on the same line (none of the 37
corpus specimens needed that, but the old tests do and nothing argues against it). A closed call at the end of
an answer cut by max tokens stays a call.

Tests: quoted calls stay text and real ones fire at every chunk split; OpenAI (whole and streamed), Anthropic
and Responses over HTTP.

serve: a request that meets a restart in progress gets an EngineDied, not an AttributeError (#1012)

Found in the live smoke: an old request that learns its engine died while restart() has already taken the
process (self.proc is None) failed in death_note() with an AttributeError, and its client got no reply at
all. death_note(), alive() and _send() now read the process once and treat None as a dead engine.

Test: after close() the death note is a sentence, alive() is False and a send raises EngineDied.

serve: a --batch request whose engine died during its prompt read ends at once instead of after 300 s (#1012)

Found in the live smoke of #1012: a long prompt being admitted when the engine is killed read its own
end-of-engine line (EngineDied), and its cleanup then drained the control lines for up to 300 s for an
end line that had been read already; the client got its 503 only after that. The cleanup now skips the
STOP and the drain when the engine process the request was sent to is gone (the server counts its engine
processes in gen, and a request notes the one it has the control lines of), and the drain polls once a
second and gives up as soon as that engine is gone.

Tests: a long read killed alone, and with short requests arriving meanwhile (it gives way and is admitted):
every request ends in a 503 within seconds, and the next request restarts the engine.

setup: a four-part hotfix version cannot break the version code

Versions are read as their first three numbers everywhere; the one place that was not (the version compiled
into an engine binary, `engine=0.1.40.1`) now accepts an optional fourth number. A test pins that a hotfix
tag keeps finding the engine zips: the checkout's v<project version> release first, the latest release second.

serve: a restart keeps the admission state, so waiting requests no longer hang or fail with ValueError (#1012)

StrataEngine.restart() runs __init__ again, which made a new condition variable, control lock, wait counter
and wait list while requests were still waiting on the old ones: they hung for good, or failed with
`list.remove(x): x not in list`. The admission state is now made once and kept; restart() wakes the waiters
when it ends. A request that waits for the control lines now ends with a clean EngineDied (503, "not sent")
when the engine is gone and nobody is starting it, keeps waiting while a restart is under way, and goes on
with the new engine when it is up. The lock is checked again after it is taken, a slot that frees itself
after a restart keeps the lists of its own process, and the wait counters cannot go below zero.

Tests (fake batch engine behind the real StrataEngine and Service): waiters during a restart are served by
the new engine (2 and 4 slots, same condition variable and lock), get a clean 503 when the engine stays down,
and when the restart itself fails; the next request restarts and is answered; the solo engine is unchanged.

serve: a tool call inside the thinking is a call only when it was an act (#804, #1058)

The #804 rescue turned any declared <tool_call> in the reasoning into a real call, so a call that was only
quoted (in a code fence, mid-sentence, in inline code, followed by more prose) ran, and so did one in a reply
cut by max tokens (47Hunter47's `rm -rf build` case). Now it must start a line (after optional whitespace),
be outside a code fence (``` or ~~~, tracked across chunks) and inline code, close with </tool_call>, and have
only whitespace or more calls after it before the end of the turn or </think>. Such calls wait until then,
and become reasoning text again when the turn ends by length, cancel or error. The decision is the same
streamed or whole. Declared calls beside an undeclared wrapper are still delivered, the wrapper stays
reasoning.

The server tells the parser how the turn ended, logs how many calls were read or kept as text, and counts
the read ones in the metrics totals (tool_calls_from_reasoning).

Tests: 37 recorded and constructed specimens (PR #525's corpus and 47Hunter47's 12 live strandings; 16 act,
21 do not) at chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 7, random and whole; fence and opener split at every position; OpenAI
(whole and streamed), Anthropic and Responses over HTTP.

serve: an engine that exits after an unread ERR line says why (#997 #890)

With "parallel": N, a batch window that fails prints its reason as an ERR
line on stdout and the engine exits with code 1. At that point every
request reads its own slot's lines, so nobody reads that ERR line, and the
server's note fell back to the log's last "strata" line (a stats line in
#997), or to "the usual cause is running out of RAM" without a log.

The pump now keeps an ERR line that was the engine's last stdout line, and
death_note gives it first. test_parallel's fake engine can fail its first
window over two slots: the note names the error.

(cherry picked from commit 9c5066303e493ba91dd09ca70d39f370d212d974)

fix(build): dma_batch.hpp copy_expert_blobs uses plain arrays (nvcc on Linux rejects its std::array locals)

dma_batch_parity.cu failed to compile on Linux/WSL (nvcc 13.0 with g++): 'template argument 2 is invalid' at the
std::array<T, cap> locals of copy_expert_blobs, whatever the form of the size (int, size_t, a literal). The engine
objects and the Windows build were not affected; the Linux tests build was.
